results.title: Welcome Helsinki | City of Helsinki
results.author: Photo: Aleksi Poutanen
highlights:
# Welcome Helsinki 

 Welcome Helsinki 

Have you recently moved to Helsinki? Welcome! On the Welcome Helsinki pages, you can find information about housing, work, education, healthcare, getting around and things to do in Helsinki.

...

## I have moved to Helsinki – what should I do next? 

After arriving in Helsinki from some other country, you need to register as a resident in Helsinki, and EU residents will need to register their EU right of residence. You may also want to open a personal bank account, register as a job seeker or apply for social benefits.

International House Helsinki (IHH) is the place to go to sort out your registrations. Use their Newcomer's Checklist to help navigate your first days and weeks in your new hometown.

- You will find information about when you should complete each step.
- The list helps you to proceed in the right order, which is very important if you wish to avoid delays in your process.
- You will also find information about the documents you need for completing each step.
- You can customise the list according to your country of origin.

## Where can I go to take care of the formalities of moving? 

Soon after moving to Helsinki from abroad, go to the International House Helsinki (IHH)! There you can complete formalities with different authorities in one place.

Make sure to plan your visit in advance, since different service desks have different opening hours. You may need to book an appointment beforehand.

If you are unsure which authorities you need to contact, go back to the Newcomer’s Checklist.

...

## How can I organise my daily life in Helsinki? 

How can you rent an apartment in Helsinki? How can you get around by public transportation or your own car? How can you find a school or a daycare place for your children, or what to do it you need a doctor? How to find a job, and what to do in your free time?

...

If you have moved to Helsinki from some other corner of Finland, find helpful information on the page When you move to Helsinki from elsewhere in Finland.

## How does Finnish society work? 

If you wish to know more in detail what kind of services are available to you in Finland and how the Finnish system works, you will find lots of helpful information on the website InfoFinland.

...

## Can I use the City’s services if I don’t speak Finnish or Swedish? 

If your mother tongue is not Finnish or Swedish, you have the right to an interpreter when you use the City’s services. The interpreter service is free. If you need an interpreter, please tell this when booking an appointment with a City service.

## Where can I ask for advice? 

If you have questions about the City services or immigration related matters, the Helsinki-info advisory service is there to help you.

results.title: City services for newcomers
highlights:
International House Helsinki (IHH) serves international newcomers in the Helsinki capital region, which consists of the cities of Helsinki, Espoo, and Vantaa.

Depending on which of these cities you live in, you can find information about the integration services they offer for international residents. Relevant links are provided below.

On the cities’ own websites, you can also find information about other municipal services they provide for their residents.

## Integration services offered by the City of Helsinki

Welcome to Helsinki is the official website for new Helsinki residents.

Use the website to learn about the City of Helsinki’s services for international newcomers, such as:

- Integration services, to help you settle into life in Helsinki
- Language learning opportunities, for Finnish and Swedish
- Employment services, for help with finding a job or starting your own business
- Other useful services and opportunities for Helsinki residents

As an international newcomer, make use of the Welcome to Helsinki site to build your life as a new Helsinki resident!

Information about City of Helsinki’s health care services you can find on this page.

...

International House Helsinki (IHH) is a service platform for immigration in the Helsinki capital region. The following public authorities and organisations are part of the IHH service network:

- The cities of Helsinki, Espoo and Vantaa
- The Finnish Immigration Service (Migri)
- The Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV)
- The Finnish Tax Administration (Vero)
- The Social Insurance Institution of Finland (Kela)
- The Finnish Centre for Pensions (ETK)
- The Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK)
- Work in Finland

results.title: Home - International House Helsinki
highlights:
# International House Helsinki

Your entry to settling in the Helsinki capital region

International House Helsinki (IHH) provides a wide range of information and public authority services to meet the needs of international newcomers in the Helsinki capital region.

IHH’s services for employers support your organisation throughout the international recruitment process, from searching for candidates to helping new international employees settle in the Helsinki capital region.

# Services for International Newcomers

### Pre-arrival Support Services

Are you considering moving to the Helsinki capital region? International House Helsinki provides pre-arrival support to help you prepare for your move and start your life in the Helsinki capital region.

### Registrations and Formalities

With International House Helsinki’s registrations and formalities services, you can take care of necessary authority steps such as registering your EU citizens’ right of residence, applying for your Finnish personal identity code, applying for your tax card, and more.

### Guidance and Settling-in Services

For general advice about life in the Helsinki capital region, International House Helsinki provides guidance and support services such as finding employment, employee rights, support for spouses, and more.

# Guides and Resources

International House Helsinki offers easy guides and resources to help international newcomers settle in the Helsinki capital region.

- The Newcomer’s Checklist
- The Newcomer’s Guide
- Housing in Helsinki: A newcomer’s guide to finding a home in the capital
- International Jobseeker’s Guide
- Guide to early childhood education and care
- Starting school in Helsinki

...

### IHH International Recruitment Services

IHH International Recruitment Services can help kickstart your organisation’s international candidate search, provide information about the settling-in services available for your employees and their family members and introduce funding measures available to support your organization.

### IHH Advisory and Counseling Services for Employers

IHH Advisory and Counseling Services can provide your organisation with support and guidance on work-based immigration and residence permits, your employees’ right to work, and your obligations as an employer of international employees.

properties.name: International House Helsinki
properties.description:
Welcome to the Helsinki capital region! International House Helsinki provides a wide range of services, information, and guidance focused on assisting international newcomers in settling in the Helsinki capital area. We also provide advisory and counseling services for companies and employers related to their international workforce. 

Whether you need to register your EU citizen's right of residence, get a tax card, get your personal identity code, or simply are looking for information about life in the capital, IHH is the gateway to starting your life here in the Helsinki capital region.

International House Helsinki is also here to support employers throughout their international recruitment journey. IHH offers counseling and advisory services for employers looking to recruit international candidates. We can support you throughout the recruitment process and advise you matter related your international workforce.

International House Helsinki is a service centre operated by the City of Helsinki. Services are provided jointly by the cities of Helsinki, Espoo and Vantaa, Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV), Finnish Tax Administration (Vero), Social Insurance Institution of Finland (Kela), Finnish Immigration Service (Migri), Work in Finland, the Finnish Centre for Pensions (ETK) and the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK). International House Helsinki was established as part of the Finnish Government’s Talent Boost Programme, funded by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment.

### Popular digital channels 

## Your profile information at one address! 

The Helsinki profile is the customer profile of a citizen using the city's digital services. It is the primary means of identification for the City's digital services. The Helsinki profile brings together the customer's personal information and contact information, as well as links to different city services, in one place. The profile allows users to manage their own data and its visibility across different services.

 Helsinki profile(Link leads to external service)

Find digital health care and social services pathways and self-care programmes. Omapolku collects all your health information and care instructions in one place, so it is always accessible.
